shortDescription: Credit Acceptance Corp. NASDAQ:CACC, a major auto lender, entered into or will enter into consent agreements with the Office of the New York Attorney General and 40 other attorneys general, the company and the NY AG said on Thursday.Under the agreement, the company will eliminate all debt owed by m…

children: with the Office of the New York Attorney General and 40 other attorneys general, the company and the NY AG said on Thursday.

Under the agreement, the company will eliminate all debt owed by more than 55,000 consumers across the nation, resulting in more than $630M in debt relief on auto loans. In addition, CACC will pay $60M in restitution to thousands of additional consumers and a $15.5M penalty to the states.
The settlement was reached without any admission of fault or wrongdoing by the company. Credit Acceptance
won't need to record additional charges beyond amounts previously accrued and disclosed in the company’s financial statements, it said.
The attorneys general alleged that Consumer Acceptance

steered tens of thousands of consumers into unaffordable loans packaged with expensive add-on products, costing consumers millions of dollars and causing some to lose their vehicles when they defaulted on loan payments, the New York Attorney General's office said.

"This resolution provides certainty for our business, our dealer partners, and the customers we serve," said Consumer Acceptance CEO Vinayak Hegde. "We believe the provisions we agreed to are constructive, customer-focused, and consistent with the direction of regulatory expectations in our industry."
stock fell 1.4% in late Thursday trading.
The lender, which specializes in subprime auto loans, said it's committed to making vehicle financing accessible to consumers who have limited alternatives.

However, New York Attorney General Letitia James said, "CAC preyed on consumers in New York and across the nation with false promises of affordable loans, only to exploit them with outrageous interest rates that ruined their credit and cost them their cars."

title: Credit Acceptance reaches over $700M settlement with states
